Summarize the following passage in detail, then list its key claims as bullet points.

The transformer architecture replaced recurrence with self-attention, letting every token attend to every other token in a sequence. During inference, generation proceeds in two phases. In the prefill phase the model processes the entire prompt in parallel, which is compute-bound and benefits from large matrix multiplications. In the decode phase the model emits one token at a time, reading all of its weights and the growing key-value cache from memory for each token, which makes decode memory-bandwidth-bound at small batch sizes. Serving systems therefore batch many concurrent requests together so that each pass over the weights produces many tokens. Techniques such as paged attention, continuous batching, prefix caching, and speculative decoding all aim to keep the accelerator busy while bounding memory use. Energy efficiency depends on the same factors: an accelerator that sits mostly idle while waiting on memory still draws substantial static power, so tokens per joule improve when batches are large enough to amortize that cost.
